newsitem.title: FRANCE: Michelin aims to expand in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Michelin aims to expand in Asia.

text.p: Michelin aims to expand its presence in Asia, which represents less than 10 percent of its turnover, Michelin's finance director said on Tuesday.
"Asia will be a favoured zone in the coming years," Eric Bourdais de Charbonniere said. "We're under-represented in this geographic area."
He said Asia had big growth potential, particularly for truck tyres, as road transport represented a bigger share of total transport in emerging economies than in developed ones.
Japan's Bridgestone was the industry leader in Asia and worldwide, according to the industry source Tire Business, Bourdais de Charbonniere told a news conference.
Tire Business last month recalculated the tyre segment of Bridgestone's activities and assigned it a global market share of 19 percent, up two points from last year.
Michelin's share has held steady at 18 percent, putting it ahead of U.S. tyremaker Goodyear with 15 percent.
Bourdais de Charbonniere said the change in rank was due to the recalculation and not to shifts in market share.
Michelin is the leader in Europe, where it generates around 55 percent of its sales. North America, where it owns Goodrich, accounts for 35 percent.
Bourdais de Charbonniere said the group's interest in diversifying its activities geographically dovetailed with its aim to reduce cyclical fluctuations.
Michelin's exposure to the European industry cycle has been reduced in the past by its important U.S. activities.

Bourdais de Charbonniere said the company was already less cyclical than it appeared, as a third of its sales were to car manufacturers, and the larger replacement market was less volatile than the car industry.
